hints: For mechanical power, use the component of force in the direction of the disc’s horizontal motion.
Resolve the 8.9 N force horizontally with cos 30°, then multiply that component by 0.60 m s⁻¹.
walkthrough: The disc moves horizontally, so only the horizontal component of force X does work on it.
Use mechanical power P = Fv with F = 8.9 cos 30° N.
To two significant figures, the rate of doing work is 4.6 W.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the mechanical-power relationship P = Fv with the force component parallel to the motion.

hints: Rearrange pressure = force / area, but first determine the total downward force exerted on the ground.
Add the disc’s weight to the downward component 8.9 sin 30° of force X, then divide that force by 3500 Pa.
walkthrough: Use p = F / A, so the required cross-sectional area is A = F / p.
The vertical component of force X acts downward: 8.9 sin 30° = 4.45 N.
The disc’s weight is mg = 0.24 × 9.81 = 2.35 N, also downward.
The combined downward force on the ground is 4.45 + 2.35 = 6.80 N.
A = 6.80 / 3500 = 1.94 × 10⁻³ m², which is 1.9 × 10⁻³ m² to two significant figures.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses p = F / A, or its rearranged form A = F / p.
Combines the downward component 8.9 sin 30° with the weight 0.24 × 9.81 to obtain about 6.80 N.
Calculates the cross-sectional area as 1.9 × 10⁻³ m².

hints: A Newton’s-third-law partner force acts on the other body and has the opposite direction to the weight of the disc.
The weight acts downward on the disc, so state the opposite vertical direction for force Y.
walkthrough: The weight is the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the disc and acts downward.
Its Newton’s-third-law partner is the gravitational force exerted by the disc on the Earth, in the opposite direction.

ai_rubric.observable: States that force Y acts upwards.

hints: Newton’s third-law forces act on two different bodies, so identify which body experiences the partner to the Earth’s force on the disc.
The disc pulls gravitationally on the body that exerts its weight.
walkthrough: The weight is the force exerted by the Earth on the disc.
The paired force is the gravitational force exerted by the disc on the Earth.
Therefore, force Y acts on the Earth.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the Earth, or planet, as the body on which force Y acts.
